name: crowagent-website-astro
//engines: R262-WEB-01. Astro 6 and 7 require Node >= 22.12.0; Astro 5 did not. This repo had NO .nvmrc, .node-version or engines field, and the Cloudflare Pages build settings are dashboard-only, so the first deploy after the Astro 7 upgrade would have failed at `npm ci` on any build image still serving Node 18 or an older 22.x — with an error about a dependency, not about Node. Pages resolves the version from NODE_VERSION, .nvmrc or .node-version (Cloudflare build-image docs), so a `.nvmrc` is committed at BOTH the repo root and `astro/` because the Pages build root is not visible from here and covering both removes the guess. 24.18.0 is the line this was actually verified on: the 33-gate chain went 33/33 on local Node 24.14.0, the Astro 5 control build passed on the same runtime, CI (.github/workflows/astro-gates.yml) uses Node 24, and 24.18.0 is preinstalled in the Cloudflare build image so it costs no download. This field is the declaration; the .nvmrc files are what Pages actually reads.
description: The modernised crowagent.ai. Isolated from the legacy tree on purpose: the live site keeps building and deploying from the repo root until this one is verified route-for-route against tag baseline-transformed-2026-08-01.

scripts.//build: R262-D-72. Was a single `&&` chain of 31 steps: the first failure stopped every gate after it from ever running, which is how check-palette-roles.js and check-render.js went unrun against WorkstationTour.astro on the build that shipped it. scripts/run-gates.mjs declares the same 31 steps in the same order and runs all of them regardless of earlier failures, prints every gate's own output plus one summary naming every pass and fail, and still exits 1 if anything failed.
scripts.//build:deploy: WHAT CLOUDFLARE PAGES RUNS. Produces the artefact and nothing else: four source guards, a type-check, the build, and the three steps that EMIT files (copy-assets, copy-cf-config, build-sitemap). It deliberately omits the ~20 browser-driving gates in `build`, because those are CERTIFICATION and belong on a developer machine. Added 2026-08-05 after the first Astro deploy failed at 35s: npm ci and astro build both succeeded and the chain died where the Playwright gates begin. Re-running certification on every deploy is slow, spends build minutes, and fails for environment reasons that say nothing about the site. Certify with `npm run build` locally BEFORE pushing; this script is not a substitute for it.
scripts.//build:deploy:pricing-parity: R262-WEB-08. check-pricing-parity.js is the ONE non-emitting gate added to the deploy chain rather than left to certification, and the reason is that it is not a certification check: it is the guard on what the site CHARGES. It costs milliseconds, drives no browser, and it is the only thing standing between a copy edit and publishing a price Stripe will not take, or publishing the Portfolio list price the owner decision forbids. The rest of the ~20 browser gates stay out of this chain for the reasons given above.
scripts.//build:deploy:brand-drift: check-brand-drift.js is the SECOND non-browser gate kept in the deploy chain rather than left to certification, for the same reason as check-pricing-parity: it is not a certification check, it is the guard on the ONE THING two separate repositories cannot otherwise keep in step. It reads two committed files, costs milliseconds, drives no browser, and it is all that stands between a palette edit here and app.crowagent.ai rendering a different brand teal — which is exactly what happened, twice, before there was a shared source.
scripts.//build:deploy:csp-required: CROWAGENT-WEB-N. check-csp-required-origins.js is the THIRD non-browser gate kept in the deploy chain rather than left to certification, and it earns that place on the same test as the other two: milliseconds, no browser, and it guards a live capability that nothing else can see. check-csp.js is deliberately NOT in this chain and could not have caught this anyway - it derives its requirements from `dist`, and Cloudflare injects the Web Analytics beacon at the edge after every build step has run, so the origin appears in no build output. The policy blocked that beacon under `enforce` from 2026-05-29 to at least 2026-08-10, 129 recorded violations, and Web Analytics recorded nothing for the whole of it while every gate stayed green. It runs LAST because it reads dist/_headers as copy-cf-config.js finally rewrote it, which is the exact bytes Cloudflare Pages will serve.
scripts.//build:deploy:sitemap-routes: check-sitemap-routes.js is the FOURTH non-browser gate kept in the deploy chain rather than left to certification, and it earns the place on the same test as the other three: milliseconds, no browser, and it guards something no other gate can see. It resolves every URL in the sitemap this chain has just emitted, plus every canonical and every structured-data page address on every built page, against the built route tree and the copied _redirects. It has to sit here and not in certification because the thing it guards is a property of the ARTEFACT, and the artefact is produced here: on 2026-08-05 the deploy source moved from the flat-file repository root to this directory-format build, which reversed the direction Cloudflare canonicalises trailing slashes in, and from that deploy until 2026-08-12 all 44 non-root sitemap URLs and all 44 self-referencing canonicals pointed at a 308. Not one URL had been edited, every gate stayed green, and Search Console would have reported 44 of 45 URLs as "Page with redirect". It runs directly after build-sitemap.js because that is the step whose output it reads.
scripts.build:deploy: node scripts/check-comment-terminators.js && node scripts/check-facts.js && node scripts/check-english.js && node scripts/check-vendor-logos.js && node scripts/check-brand-drift.js && astro check && astro build && node scripts/copy-assets.js && node scripts/copy-cf-config.js && node scripts/build-sitemap.js && node scripts/check-sitemap-routes.js && node scripts/check-pricing-parity.js && node scripts/check-csp-required-origins.js
